questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where I knew there would be a big Erasmus network. The prospect of being part of a large and diverse community through Erasmus was appealing as it meant I would have the opportunity to meet people from various cultural backgrounds. This, I believed, would not only enhance my social experience but also contribute to a broader and more global perspective in my studies. Of course, the availability and quality of programs were also important factor for my study destination. Additionally, I considered the cost of living, aiming for affordability. Lastly, having a warm climate was a welcomed bonus for me in choosing a study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Initially, it felt like a jungle. Navigating through a different website and figuring out how the foreign university structures its courses and follows its academic calendar posed challenges. However, once the system's ways were understood, it became relatively manageable to comprehend.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received all information on mail which worked well. There was also a dedicated mobility office for exchange students where one could drop in and ask questions. They arranged two types of introduction/orientation meetings. One for all exchange students collectively and one for your specific faculty in which you were enrolled.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I became a member of several Facebook groups such as Erasmus in Barcelona groups, "Danskere i Barcelona" and Barcelona rooms groups where I successfully, three months prior to my exchange, found three roomies I could live with.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Choosing to live off-campus provides a selection of housing options, not only in terms of cost but also in the arrangements with roommates. However, make sure that it isn't too complicated to get to your university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
They had a link for course information and a link for course schedules which was useful to finding information. However, these links had to be accessed through the website; you couldn't copy and save them for future reference because they would become invalid after some time. And finding the links on the website in the first place could be a little bit difficult and hard to remember for subsequent use. 

The registration process for courses operated on a specific timeframe, utilising a first-come, first-served basis. This created a stressful experience, with the website crashing multiple times during the initial registration window. Fortunately, after 15 minutes, the system stabilised, allowing me to successfully register for my courses using the guidance provided in the PDF document sent to students before the registration period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could contact them via email or phone, and they were helpful in assisting me and redirecting my call to the appropriate person when I reached out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fortunately, after the system remained stable beyond the initial 15 minutes, I was able to successfully enrol in the courses of my choice. I recall only one course being already full, but luckily, my backup option proved effective. Upon arrival and completion of the first week of school, there was the option to add/drop courses, providing convenience. However, it also introduced a bit of chaos as, within such a short timeframe (one week), it was challenging to gauge the courses accurately. Nevertheless, they opened a new window for adding and dropping courses in the subsequent weeks, which was a positive aspect. Moreover, UPF followed a trimester system, whereas you may be accustomed to semesters at your home institution. Consequently, you were required to complete 30 ECTS credits at a university that typically operates with 20 ECTS credits per trimester. This translated to a substantial workload for me, involving the study of six courses as opposed to the three or four courses that others at the university undertook.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would strongly find a way to not have 30 ECTS credits workload at a university that operates with less per semester/trimester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty level was acceptable, slightly easier than what I was accustomed to at my home institution. However, the trade-off was a significantly heavier workload. Attendance was mandatory, and in most courses, there were multiple assignments to submit. This workload compensated for the comparatively lighter course content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A notable difference was evident in the approach to class engagement and participation. The host institution placed a stronger emphasis on interactive learning methods, encompassing obligatory class discussions, group projects, and presentations. Thus, UPF demanded a more intensive commitment, with a requirement for regular class attendance and active involvement in various academic activities. However, the readings were not as extensive and weighty as those at UCPH but being able to structure your own time and way of learning as you can at home, is not so much of an option at UPF. To say it shortly, it is like doing high school all over again

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They have several faculties and campuses and you can enrol at all of them (even despite the fact that the specific agreement between UCPH and UPF is with the Humanities faculty) as long as you can make it fit in your calendar and there's are spots free of course. My courses were good and I can recommend them. Finding courses that matches your liking should not be too difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter many unforeseen expenses. I prioritised experiences such as traveling and exploring different places, which, naturally, can be quite costly. However, it's worth noting that pickpocketing is prevalent in Barcelona. I know of a lot of people who had their phones and belongings stolen, so it's crucial to be cautious as this could result in unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I thought groceries would be cheaper than in DK but it was almost the same. Going out for dinner er was also cheaper in general than in DK but not a lot cheaper.

questions.answer: I didn't join any clubs etc. so I am not the right one to ask but I think there were different possibilities of joining different things but I am not too sure.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Absolutely, make sure to explore the Gaudi buildings, Montjuic mountain, and wander through the streets of Eixample and Passeig de Gracia, among others. I also took the opportunity to travel to Marrakech, leveraging the proximity to other new destinations compared to being in Denmark. Additionally, I explored Costa Brava (coast region a small drive north from BCN) and Sitges (a cute small city an hr drive from BCN) during my time in Spain. I also saw El Clásico in Barcelona and took a trip to Madrid as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Considering the challenges of relocating from familiar surroundings, friends, and family, the process of settling in Barcelona was fairly smoothly. While the culture and overall environment weren't drastically different from home, there were still numerous opportunities to learn and experience new things.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the Erasmus network to socialise with other students. UPF has one of the best Erasmus initiatives and activities from trips, parties and learning Spanish/Catalan (from own experience and from what I have heard from other students studying at other universities in BCN).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way they structured the school was definitely the hardest thing for me to adapt to. Many of the locals did not speak English which can also be a bit challenging but you always find a way!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: In Spain, punctuality and adherence to meeting times are not as strict, which can create a more laid-back atmosphere once you get accustomed to the rhythm. The tapas culture, characterized by the practice of sharing, is also a pleasant and distinct experience compared to Denmark, where individuals typically order one dish per person.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Workload is a lot and schedule is full if you take 30 ECTS.

Barcelona offers the convenience of having everything nearby! Make the most of it. The city boasts the sea, mountains within the city and other stunning landscapes just a few hours' (even just 1 hr) drive away.

If you don't know anyone going to Barcelona, join their Erasmus network.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Being independent and overcoming obstacles coming out stronger on the other side every time is so rewarding in the end – because you do face challenges when you go on exchange but everyone else is facing their own challenges and often times the same as you about going on exchange.

Meeting a lot of different people. I had a group project in every course I took (just a single or two in each) which meant I was in different groups learning to work with different people and adapting to different work ethics. This experience was actually quite educational and enriching.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling lonely at times and figuring out how to handle 30 ECTS credits load.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
